text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) wrapped up a 10-day staff visit to Lithuania on Wednesday, praising the country as one of the best former communist reform economies and urging the government to stay on course.
"Lithuania has been one of the best reforming transition economies," Domenico Fanizza, the IMF's resident representative in Lithuania, told Reuters.
The staff visit paves the way for the last distribution of $15 million of a three-year Extended Fund Facility arrangement worth a total of $200 million.
"The performance (by Lithuania) under the arrangement has been very positive," Fanizza said.
Fanizza said the IMF praised the current government for fiscal restraint and its efforts to raise tax collection but stressed the need for "second-generation" reforms.
"We stressed the need to press ahead with privatisation and structural reform," Fanizza said, adding that strengthening of the banking sector and legal systems would be key in the future.

In the fall an IMF mission is expected to take up with the government the Fund's future relations with Lithuania, which may take the form of a formal arrangement or a looser agreement involving surveillance of the reform process.
